title: Strict scalar pullback cone maps and their derived naturality
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $W=X,Y$, $F=E,L$, $m\ge1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the quotient maps $\iota_m:\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m\to\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ and $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For any cochain complex $P$ of $R_Y$-modules put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$; tensor products are sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For an $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$-complex $M$ put
$$D^F_m(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD^F_m(M)\to\prod_mD^F_m(M))[-1],$$
using module inverse image $g_{F,m}^*=g^{-1}(-)\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{F,Y,m}}B_{F,X,m}$, coefficient structure maps [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], restriction of scalars and quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. There is a natural strict tower map $d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to D^L_m(Q)$ uniquely specified on local tensor generators by
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto(g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)).$$
These formulas are balanced, commute with the cochain differentials and every quotient transition, and are natural in all chain maps $P\to P'$. Since $S_X$ is a finite free $R_X$-module [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison], the canonical tensor/product maps are isomorphisms, independent of a choice of finite free basis of $S_X$ over $R_X$, and identify $A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with the Roos cone of $D^E_\bullet(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$. The induced chain map $\delta_P$ to $A_L(Q)$ sends both cone coordinates by $\prod_m d_m$. On flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex], these chain maps descend to a natural transformation
$$C_X Lg_E^*\longrightarrow Lg_L^* C_Y,\qquad C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W,$$
with representative $[\delta_P]$ under the canonical comparison isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined, lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. In particular the represented morphism is independent of the K-flat resolution and natural for arbitrary derived morphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For $E\subset L\subset F$ the level maps and cone maps compose to those for $E\subset F$ after the canonical tensor associators; for $L=E$ they are identities under the tensor unit identifications.

proof.text: The existing additive Roos map is natural and has both prescribed coordinates. Product preservation makes its product comparison invertible. In degree i the cone is a binary biproduct of the product in degrees i and i-1. Additivity and the two invertible product components therefore make the Roos comparison invertible. Assemble these components into kappa. Both coordinate formulas give its required normalization. If another kappa has the normalization, compose its components with mappingCocone.id_X; agreement on fst and snd proves equality of the complex maps and of the natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Put delta = kappa followed by the Roos image of d. Good complexes localize to the entire derived category by the existing good-complex localization theorem. On good representatives use the E-pullback comparison, then the X scalar counit, then the localization of delta, producing a. The Y scalar counit and the L-pullback comparison form an isomorphism b from the restricted target derived functor. Fully faithful precomposition with the good localization lifts a followed by b inverse to a unique tau. Its component equation is precisely the published descent equation. Conversely any tau satisfying descent has its restriction determined by cancellation of b, proving uniqueness. This handles all derived morphisms directly, without requiring an additional explicit homotopy descent argument.

proof.text: Assemble d, kappa, tau and their equations into strict cone data. For any two data first use uniqueness of the tower component, then uniqueness of the two-coordinate cone isomorphism, and finally uniqueness of derived descent. Proof irrelevance identifies the equation fields; hence the data type is a subsingleton.

lean.statement:
theorem scalarPullbackStrictConeNaturality
    {X Y : AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.{t}} (g : X ⟶ Y)
    (_hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.residueField x))
    (_hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.residueField y)) :
    (∀ K : ℕ → CochainComplex (integralTowerModules l E X) ℤ,
      IsIso (scalarPullbackProductMap l E L ι X K)) ∧
    (∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory,
      integralOperationsGoodComplex l L Y
        ((completedOrdinaryScalarComplex l E L ι Y).obj P.obj)) ∧
    (∀ P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E Y).FullSubcategory,
      IsIso (completedScalarCounit l E L ι X
        ((integralOperationsPullbackComplexFunctor l E g).obj P.obj))) ∧
    Nonempty (ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E L ι g) ∧
    Subsingleton (ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E L ι g) ∧
    (∀ D : ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E L ι g,
      ScalarPullbackCompositionFormula l E L ι g D) ∧
    (∀ D : ScalarPullbackStrictConeData l E E (AlgHom.id ℚ_[l] E) g,
      ScalarPullbackUnitFormula l E g D)
lean.note: The main proof assembles the unique balanced tower map, a proved generic two-coordinate cone isomorphism, and the proved unique derived descent in ScalarPullbackUniqueDerivedDescent. Finite-free scalar properties are proved separately. Only the strict tower construction and chain composition/unit calculations remain as two smaller obligations. The original auxiliary definitions are publicly re-exported unchanged from ScalarPullbackStrictConeData.
